output.title: Why data cleaning is not enough
output.body:
Data cleaning helps, but it is not the whole workflow. If your team spends time fixing fields and still has to make the same downstream decisions by hand, you have only solved the input side. The real question is simple: what still needs human judgment after the data is clean?

That matters because many small-business workflows break in two places: messy inputs and decision handling. Cleaning addresses the first. It does not remove the second. If a clean row still needs someone to categorise it, route it, approve it, or decide whether it is an exception, the manual work is still there. Software is great at repeating rules; it is less helpful when the rule is “have a look and see.”

A practical next step is to map one repeating workflow as input → decision → output. Write down the steps, then mark which ones are rules-based and which ones need judgment or sign-off. If you find that cleaned data still leaves a long tail of manual decisions, that boundary is often where automation fits. For higher-risk steps, keep human approval in place. Bareni’s self-built demo shows rule checks, exception handling, and human-only approval as controls, not as a replacement for it.

Start by mapping the decision layer, not by buying another cleanup tool.
